articles.title: How to turn the dregs of a ketchup bottle into a classic Marie Rose dressing – recipe | Waste not
articles.summary: Shake up the remnants of a bottle of ketchup with a splash of sprits, a heap of mayonnaise and a few other simple additions, and turn it into one of the culinary world’s most famous sauces.
body: M y new favourite preparation for sauces, marinades and dressings is in a near-empty jar, tub or bottle, so I can upcycle all the remains. Rather than washing it and putting it in the recycling, I instead add a few store-cupboard ingredients to create a dressing or sauce, often re-exploring classics such as a retro Marie Rose sauce or my yoghurt-pot chicken. It’s a convenient way to use up the last dregs of a ketchup bottle, for instance, which often seems to harbour exactly the right amount of sauce.

My Marie Rose recipe is inspired by the one in Simon Hopkinson and Lindsey Bareham ’s 1997 The Prawn Cocktail Years. It’s wonderfully simple, with the sophisticated addition of a dash of cognac, though other recipes use brandy. I had neither, however, but I did have some sweet vermouth left over, which worked exceptionally well, so feel free to experiment with whatever spirits you have to hand – vodka, for instance, works brilliantly, and gives the sauce a nice kick.

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s flamboyant, fun style: ‘I’m not a fashion icon; I’m an eyesore’
articles.summary: With her gaudy rhinestones and ever mushrooming hair, the country star pioneered a new vision of femininity. Dolly Parton, country star, actor and philanthropist, dies aged 80. Dolly Parton – a life in pictures. Parton’s peerless career turned country music cliches inside out.
body: Dolly Parton ’s voluminous hair and rhinestone-festooned outfits were so essential to her fame that her quips about her appearance have become almost as well-known as her lyrics.
“It costs a lot of money to look this cheap” is perhaps her most memorable quotation, and is typical of the self-depreciating wit she employed to talk about her appearance.

She wrote about her style in her songs, too, from her 1967 hit Dumb Blonde to 2008’s Backwoods Barbie, though in reality there was nothing cheap, or dumb, about her image. With huge blond status wigs – Tennessee by way of the court of Versailles – a fondness for glitter and high heels and tightly cut clothes that showed off her exaggerated proportions, she made herself as recognizable as Coca-Cola while employing and subverting the tropes of femininity and of country music.

Parton never failed to poke fun at her own appearance. Her hair was a “fire hazard”, she would say, or “I’m not a fashion icon; I’m an eyesore” – but her look was highly deliberate. Never once did she waver from the aesthetic she described to Allure in 2020 as “gaudy, flamboyant, fun, comfortable – for me – noticeable”.
points: With her gaudy rhinestones and ever mushrooming hair, the country star pioneered a new vision of femininity.

articles.title: A moment that changed me: I sought out rejection. Instead, strangers met me with profound generosity
articles.summary: As I turned 21, fear was holding me back. So I decided to face it headfirst. It taught me that courage leads to connection – and people who owe you nothing can be astonishingly kind. In May 2024, I decided to spend 30 days getting rejected on purpose. At first, it sounded ridiculous.
body: At first, it sounded ridiculous. After all, most people spend their lives actively trying to avoid rejection – and I was deciding to walk, full force, towards it. But it had become obvious, as I turned 21, that my terror of being rejected was holding me back.

For over two years, I’d stayed in a relationship I knew wasn’t working, all too aware that the alternative – dating – would likely be riddled with rejection. On social occasions I often felt absent, focusing solely on not seeming weird or doing anything that might make others laugh at me. And in my first proper job, as a social media manager, I would talk myself out of opportunities that would put me in the spotlight and might have given me a chance to shine.
So I promised myself I’d stop hiding from rejection for one month and see what happened. After a lifetime of worrying what people thought about me, I knew that only radical action would work.
points: It taught me that courage leads to connection – and people who owe you nothing can be astonishingly kind.

articles.title: The row over Rutland: can England’s smallest county survive?
articles.summary: Its council is due to merge with Leicestershire’s in 2028, and some locals are incensed. Can the county hold on to its ceremonial status – and biggest selling point? Mysterious disappearances have been taking place lately in Rutland, an East Midlands pocket between Leicestershire, Lincolnshire and…
body: The area’s MP, the Conservative Alicia Kearns, is “not sure” what the motivation behind the thefts is. But they are certainly a fitting metaphor for Rutland’s disappearing status: its council is due to merge with Leicestershire county council in spring 2028.

“The joke goes: ‘Rutland is England 50 years ago,’” says Kearns when we meet at the county’s most famous landmark, the UK’s largest reservoir by surface area, Rutland Water, home to the Rutland Osprey Project. She tells me about the county’s farming community, its tradition of Friday shoots that supply the local pubs with game, its pride in local businesses. So resistant are Rutlanders to some aspects of modernity, “we were the last county to have a McDonald’s built”, she says. Even when it did finally arrive, in 2020, the decision “was really controversial”.

articles.title: London’s Fast Approaching Fall Won’t Keep Millie Bobby Brown Out of Her Capris
articles.summary: Millie Bobby Brown stepped out in London on Monday for dinner at Dorian with her husband, Jake Bongiovi, and her famous father-in-law Jon Bongiovi.
body: While fall approaches fast and temperatures are inching downward, Millie Bobby Brown is staying committed to her cropped pants.

She wore a pair of black and white polka-dot capri pants from Princess Polly, paired with a fine knit beige Comma cardigan over a black tank top, Reformation’s heeled and strappy black patent Mallori sandals, and a mini black handbag. For jewelry, a pair of Mejuri Ines drop studs and her cushion cut diamond engagement ring. Her long brunette hair was up in a loose ponytail.

M.B.B—who recently appeared with her miniature poodle Winnie as part of Vogue’s Dogue—posed gamely with her father-in-law and husband when exiting the restaurant. Jake, for his part, wore a burnt orange v-neck knit over a white shirt, collar nonchalantly popped, with cream pants and white adidas sneakers. It was a typical, subtly coordinating couple style moment for the young married couple. Jon wore the typical dad uniform: a black bomber, black t-shirt, and tapered blue jeans.

articles.title: 15 Charming Dolly Parton Quotes on Life, Love, and Everything In Between
articles.summary: The country music icon Dolly Parton has passed away at the age of age: her love of dazzling rhinestones and great bon mots remain gifts to us all.
body: Dolly Parton, the celebrated country singer, humanitarian, and bedazzled, bleach-blonde glamazon, has died at the age of 80. Tributes have poured in from across the music, fashion, and film worlds, with heartfelt reflections on Parton’s humor, spirit, and decades-spanning musical legacy.

“A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family,” said a statement posted to Parton’s Instagram.
“I can’t even tell you how many times I’ve thought to myself, ‘what would Dolly do?’” Cyndi Lauper wrote in her own tribute.

Over the years, culture has attempted to document the magic: there was Dolly Parton’s America, a podcast devoted to her rise; a Netflix show, Heartstrings; a musical and a book, Songteller: My Life in Lyrics; all topped off with a festive movie, Christmas on the Square. Decades after she first stepped into the spotlight, the queen of country music (and her rhinestone-embellished attire) has continued to inspire a love that knows no bounds.
points: The country music icon Dolly Parton has passed away at the age of age: her love of dazzling rhinestones and great bon mots remain gifts to us all.

articles.title: 9 Best Places to Travel in Fall, From Upstate Cabins to French Vineyards
articles.summary: Wondering what the best places to travel in the fall are? From countryside retreats to city escapes, these nine destinations are a good place to start.
body: Amber-colored foliage, winding vineyards ready for harvest, a slight chill in the air that lends itself perfectly to a long day of sightseeing (made even more perfect when it ends with a cozy bowl of risotto)—autumn may actually be the perfect travel season. Whether you want to book a country escape or lean toward a packed city itinerary, the best places to travel in fall are hardly a one-size-fits-all list. Neither are our recommendations: We included destinations far and wide, with plenty of stays that speak to a range of travel styles.

Nature lovers will find lots to occupy themselves with in the sprawling Scottish Highlands or the lakeside hikes of upstate New York. Though if your idea of the great outdoors leans more to swirling glasses of Merlot among unending rows of grapes, a trip to Bordeaux or Tuscany might be more your speed. For a dose of city charm, head to Kyoto to get your fill of historic architecture and buzzing markets. And if you’re still not sure—well, you know what they say about Paris.

articles.title: How to Party Like a Local in Mykonos, According to a Seasoned Veteran
articles.summary: A lifelong regular’s guide to choosing the right coast, landing in the part of the venue you meant to book, and getting home before the taxis disappear.
body: The sun starts to set on Little Venice and its windmills in Mykonos Town, one of many popular vistas on the island.

Now craft beer is brewed on the island, and casual Chora bars pour proper cocktails into paper cups and send revelers off into the night. Greek musicians share the calendar with international DJs, periodically reminding Mykonos of which country it belongs to. The familiar bottle-service caricature leaves out the drag stages of the old port and the smaller rooms where a night can change direction without a reservation. Prices remain high and the roads maddening, but few Mediterranean islands offer so many convincing ways to reach sunrise. After enough summers on both sides of the nap, I have settled on seven rules that every visitor needs to know.
Many of the outdoor tables in Little Venice are just inches from the tide.
